articles.x: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, from the tribe of Quraysh, from Banu Hashim.

b.v: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Mecca in the Year of the Elephant, from the tribe of Quraysh, from Banu Hashim. His father Abdullah died before his birth, and his mother Aminah died while he was still young. His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib took him in, then his uncle Abu Talib, so he grew up an orphan, and Allah sheltered and cared for him. He worked as a shepherd and then in trade, and he was known among his people for truthfulness and trustworthiness.

articles.x: He ﷺ married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid after she was impressed by his trustworthiness in her trade, and she was the first to believe in him.

b.v: He ﷺ married Khadijah bint Khuwaylid after she was impressed by his trustworthiness in her trade, and she was the first to believe in him. He witnessed Quraysh's rebuilding of the Kaaba, and they appointed him to arbitrate the placing of the Black Stone, so he spared their bloodshed with his wisdom. He used to worship in seclusion in the Cave of Hira and kept away from his people's idols, and he was given the title 'the Truthful, the Trustworthy' (al-Sadiq al-Amin) before he was sent as a prophet.

articles.t: The Beginning of Revelation and the Prophethood
articles.x: Gabriel descended upon the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Hira when he was forty years old, and recited to him the first words revealed of the Qur'an: 'اقرأ باسم ربك الذي…

b.v: Gabriel descended upon the Prophet ﷺ in the Cave of Hira when he was forty years old, and recited to him the first words revealed of the Qur'an: 'اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق'. He returned to Khadijah frightened, and she reassured and comforted him, then took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who gave him the glad tidings that he was the prophet of this nation. Then the revelation paused for a period, after which it resumed continuously with the command to warn and call to Islam.

articles.x: The Prophet ﷺ called to Islam secretly for about three years, fearing the violence of Quraysh.

b.v: The Prophet ﷺ called to Islam secretly for about three years, fearing the violence of Quraysh. The first to believe in him were the foremost believers: Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Ali, and Zayd ibn Harithah, and then people entered the religion individually. He took the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam as a center for teaching the Muslims and reciting the Qur'an in secret.

articles.t: The Public Call and the Persecution by Quraysh
articles.x: Allah commanded His Prophet to proclaim the call openly: 'فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين', so he called his people from Mount Safa.

b.v: Allah commanded His Prophet to proclaim the call openly: 'فاصدع بما تؤمر وأعرض عن المشركين', so he called his people from Mount Safa. The polytheists became his enemies and harmed the weak among the believers, such as Bilal and the family of Yasir, and they besieged Banu Hashim in the mountain pass (al-Shi'b). The Muslims endured the harm, remaining firm upon their religion despite the torture and the boycott.

articles.x: When the persecution by Quraysh intensified, the Prophet ﷺ permitted a group of his companions to migrate to Abyssinia, where there was a just king under whom no one was…

b.v: When the persecution by Quraysh intensified, the Prophet ﷺ permitted a group of his companions to migrate to Abyssinia, where there was a just king under whom no one was wronged. They migrated in two waves, and they remained firm in their religion before the Negus when Quraysh sent someone to demand their return. The Negus protected them after hearing verses from Surat Maryam concerning Jesus and Mary.

articles.t: The Night Journey and the Ascension (Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj)
articles.x: Allah took His Prophet ﷺ on a night journey from the Sacred Masjid to the Farthest Masjid, then he was ascended to the highest heavens.

b.v: Allah took His Prophet ﷺ on a night journey from the Sacred Masjid to the Farthest Masjid, then he was ascended to the highest heavens. He saw of the great signs of his Lord, and the five daily prayers were made obligatory upon him on that night. It was a source of strength for the Prophet ﷺ after the Year of Sorrow, in which he lost his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib.

articles.k: The Beginning of the Medinan Period
articles.x: After the Ansar pledged allegiance to him at al-Aqabah, Allah permitted the Muslims to migrate to Yathrib.

b.v: After the Ansar pledged allegiance to him at al-Aqabah, Allah permitted the Muslims to migrate to Yathrib. The Prophet ﷺ migrated with Abu Bakr, and they hid in the Cave of Thawr until Allah surrounded them with His protection and saved them from Quraysh. He arrived in Medina, built the masjid, established brotherhood between the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and founded the Islamic state, with which the Hijri calendar began.

articles.x: In Ramadan of the second year after the Hijrah, the Muslims, numbering about three hundred and some odd, met the army of Quraysh, which reached about a thousand…

b.v: In Ramadan of the second year after the Hijrah, the Muslims, numbering about three hundred and some odd, met the army of Quraysh, which reached about a thousand fighters. Allah gave victory to the believers despite their small number and reinforced them with angels, and the chiefs of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl, were killed. Badr was the Day of the Criterion (Yawm al-Furqan), by which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood.

articles.x: Quraysh set out in the third year to avenge those killed at Badr, and the two groups met at Mount Uhud.

b.v: Quraysh set out in the third year to avenge those killed at Badr, and the two groups met at Mount Uhud. The Muslims were about to be victorious until the archers left their positions out of desire for spoils, so the polytheists encircled them, and the Muslims were struck; the Prophet's ﷺ face was wounded, and his uncle Hamzah was martyred. Allah revealed verses to console the believers and teach them lessons of obedience and steadfastness.

articles.x: Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews formed a confederacy to annihilate the Muslims in the fifth year, so Salman al-Farisi suggested digging a trench around Medina.

b.v: Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews formed a confederacy to annihilate the Muslims in the fifth year, so Salman al-Farisi suggested digging a trench around Medina. The confederates besieged Medina for days in severe cold until the believers were shaken and hearts reached their throats. Allah then sent a wind and unseen soldiers, and He repelled the confederates in disappointment without major fighting.

articles.x: The Prophet ﷺ set out with his companions intending to perform Umrah, but Quraysh blocked them at Hudaybiyyah, so a treaty was made with a ten-year truce.

b.v: The Prophet ﷺ set out with his companions intending to perform Umrah, but Quraysh blocked them at Hudaybiyyah, so a treaty was made with a ten-year truce. The companions pledged allegiance to the Prophet under the tree — the Pledge of Ridwan — when a rumor spread that Uthman had been killed. Although the terms of the treaty appeared unjust, Allah named it a manifest victory, for people found safety and Islam spread during the time of the truce.

articles.x: When Quraysh broke their treaty, the Prophet ﷺ marched with ten thousand Muslims and conquered Mecca in Ramadan of the eighth year without any notable fighting.

b.v: When Quraysh broke their treaty, the Prophet ﷺ marched with ten thousand Muslims and conquered Mecca in Ramadan of the eighth year without any notable fighting. He entered it humbly, with his head lowered in gratitude to Allah, and he smashed the idols around the Kaaba and forgave the people of Mecca, saying: 'اذهبوا فأنتم الطلقاء'. So people entered the religion of Allah in throngs.

articles.x: The Prophet ﷺ performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year and delivered a comprehensive sermon to the people at Arafat, in which he affirmed the sanctity of…

b.v: The Prophet ﷺ performed the Farewell Pilgrimage in the tenth year and delivered a comprehensive sermon to the people at Arafat, in which he affirmed the sanctity of blood, wealth, and people's rights. Then was revealed to him: 'اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم'. He then fell ill and returned to his Lord in Rabi' al-Awwal of the eleventh year in Medina, after having conveyed the message and fulfilled the trust, and he was buried in the chamber of Aisha.

articles.x: The first of mankind and the father of the prophets. Allah created him with His own Hand, breathed into him from His spirit, and made the angels prostrate to him.

b.v: The first of mankind and the father of the prophets. Allah created him with His own Hand, breathed into him from His spirit, and made the angels prostrate to him. He settled him in Paradise and taught him all the names. He tested him with a prohibition regarding a tree, and he ate from it through Satan's whispering, so Allah accepted his repentance and chose him, then sent him down to the earth to populate it with his offspring.
Al-Baqara 2:30-37; Al-A'raaf 7:11-25; Taa-Haa 20:115-122

articles.x: A truthful prophet among the earliest of the prophets, described by Allah with patience and truthfulness, and raised by Him to a high station.

b.v: A truthful prophet among the earliest of the prophets, described by Allah with patience and truthfulness, and raised by Him to a high station. He is mentioned in the Qur'an in connection with the patient and righteous.
Maryam 19:56-57; Al-Anbiyaa 21:85-86

articles.x: The first of the messengers to the people of the earth. He called his people to the oneness of Allah for a thousand years less fifty, yet only a few believed.

b.v: The first of the messengers to the people of the earth. He called his people to the oneness of Allah for a thousand years less fifty, yet only a few believed. Allah commanded him to build the ark, so He drowned the disbelievers in the flood and saved the believers with him.

articles.x: He was sent to the people of 'Aad, who dwelt in al-Ahqaf and were possessors of strength and mighty structures.

b.v: He was sent to the people of 'Aad, who dwelt in al-Ahqaf and were possessors of strength and mighty structures. He called them to worship Allah alone and to reject idols. They denied him and were arrogant, so Allah destroyed them with a furious, raging wind, and saved Hud and those who believed with him.

articles.x: He was sent to the people of Thamud, who carved out the mountains as houses. He called them to the oneness of Allah and brought them the sign of the she-camel.

b.v: He was sent to the people of Thamud, who carved out the mountains as houses. He called them to the oneness of Allah and brought them the sign of the she-camel. They hamstrung the she-camel and denied him, so the Shout and the tremor seized them, and they lay lifeless, fallen prostrate in their homes.

articles.x: The Friend of the Most Merciful and the leader of the monotheists, he smashed the idols of his people and Allah saved him from the fire, and he migrated for the sake of…

b.v: The Friend of the Most Merciful and the leader of the monotheists, he smashed the idols of his people and Allah saved him from the fire, and he migrated for the sake of Allah. He built the Ka'bah together with his son Isma'il, and was tried with the sacrifice of his son, so Allah ransomed him with a great sacrifice, and placed prophethood among his descendants.
Al-An'aam 6:74-83; Al-Anbiyaa 21:51-70; As-Saaffaat 37:99-113; Al-Baqara 2:124-129

articles.x: The nephew of Ibrahim (son of his brother), he was sent to the people of Sodom who committed indecency with men, so he called them to abandon evil and worship Allah.

b.v: The nephew of Ibrahim (son of his brother), he was sent to the people of Sodom who committed indecency with men, so he called them to abandon evil and worship Allah. They persisted in their misguidance, so Allah saved him and his family except his wife, and destroyed the town by overturning it and raining stones upon it.

articles.x: The firstborn son of Ibrahim, he was true to his promise and was a Messenger and Prophet, and he submitted to Allah's command when the sacrifice was presented to him.

b.v: The firstborn son of Ibrahim, he was true to his promise and was a Messenger and Prophet, and he submitted to Allah's command when the sacrifice was presented to him. He shared with his father in raising the foundations of the Sacred House, and he commanded his family to prayer and zakat.
As-Saaffaat 37:101-107; Al-Baqara 2:125-129; Maryam 19:54-55; Al-Anbiyaa 21:85-86

articles.x: The son of Ibrahim, glad tidings of him were given in the old age of his parents, and Allah made him a Prophet among the righteous.

b.v: The son of Ibrahim, glad tidings of him were given in the old age of his parents, and Allah made him a Prophet among the righteous. Allah granted him Ya'qub, and placed prophethood among his descendants.
Hud 11:71-73; As-Saaffaat 37:112-113; Al-Anbiyaa 21:72; Maryam 19:49

articles.x: The son of Ishaq, also called Isra'il, a Prophet from the descendants of Ibrahim whom Allah chose.

b.v: The son of Ishaq, also called Isra'il, a Prophet from the descendants of Ibrahim whom Allah chose. He was patient over the loss of his son Yusuf until his eyes turned white from grief, and he enjoined his sons to monotheism at his death.
Al-Baqara 2:132-133; Yusuf 12:6; Yusuf 12:83-87; Al-Anbiyaa 21:72

articles.x: The son of Ya'qub (Jacob), he saw a vision of the stars prostrating to him, so his brothers envied him and threw him into the well.

b.v: The son of Ya'qub (Jacob), he saw a vision of the stars prostrating to him, so his brothers envied him and threw him into the well. He was tried with slavery and imprisonment, then Allah established him over the treasuries of Egypt, so he forgave his brothers and reunited his family, and his story is the best of stories.
سورة يوسف 12 كاملة

articles.x: A patient prophet whom Allah tried in his body, his wealth, and his family, so he bore it with beautiful patience and complained only to his Lord.

b.v: A patient prophet whom Allah tried in his body, his wealth, and his family, so he bore it with beautiful patience and complained only to his Lord. Allah answered his prayer, removed his affliction, and restored to him his family and the like of them along with them, and he was indeed an excellent, oft-returning servant.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:83-84; Saad 38:41-44

articles.x: He was sent to the people of Madyan and the Companions of the Thicket, who gave short measure and weight, so he called them to monotheism and to justice in dealings.

b.v: He was sent to the people of Madyan and the Companions of the Thicket, who gave short measure and weight, so he called them to monotheism and to justice in dealings. They denied him and threatened him, so the tremor seized them, along with the punishment of the Day of the Shadow (the overshadowing cloud), and Allah saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him.

articles.x: The one to whom Allah spoke directly (Kalim Allah), he grew up in the house of Pharaoh, then Allah sent him as a messenger to him and gave him nine clear signs.

b.v: The one to whom Allah spoke directly (Kalim Allah), he grew up in the house of Pharaoh, then Allah sent him as a messenger to him and gave him nine clear signs. He saved the Children of Israel and split the sea for them, drowning Pharaoh, and Allah revealed to him the Torah and spoke to him at Mount Tur.
Al-Qasas 28:3-43; Taa-Haa 20:9-98; Al-A'raaf 7:103-156

articles.x: The brother and support of Musa, Musa asked his Lord to make him his minister (helper), so Allah answered and granted him to him as a prophet.

b.v: The brother and support of Musa, Musa asked his Lord to make him his minister (helper), so Allah answered and granted him to him as a prophet. He assisted Musa in calling Pharaoh, and succeeded him among his people, denouncing them for worshipping the calf.
Taa-Haa 20:29-36; Al-A'raaf 7:142; Al-Qasas 28:34; Maryam 19:53

articles.x: A righteous prophet whom Allah mentioned among the patient, good people and admitted into His mercy.

b.v: A righteous prophet whom Allah mentioned among the patient, good people and admitted into His mercy. The Qur'an did not elaborate on his story, and limited itself to praising him for patience and righteousness.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:85-86; Saad 38:48

articles.x: A prophet-king to whom Allah gave the Psalms (Zabur), wisdom, and decisive speech, and subjected the mountains and birds to glorify with him.

b.v: A prophet-king to whom Allah gave the Psalms (Zabur), wisdom, and decisive speech, and subjected the mountains and birds to glorify with him. He softened iron for him, he killed Goliath (Jalut), and he was ever-turning to Allah, strong in worship, and just in judgment.
Saad 38:17-26; Al-Anbiyaa 21:78-80; Saba 34:10-11; Al-Baqara 2:251

articles.x: Son of David; Allah gave him a mighty kingdom, taught him the language of birds, and subjected the jinn and the wind to him.

b.v: Son of David; Allah gave him a mighty kingdom, taught him the language of birds, and subjected the jinn and the wind to him. He conversed with the hoopoe and corresponded with the Queen of Sheba, who then submitted (to Islam), and he was a grateful, ever-turning servant.

articles.x: One of the messengers; he was sent to his people, calling them to worship Allah and forbidding them from worshipping the idol 'Ba'l'.

b.v: One of the messengers; he was sent to his people, calling them to worship Allah and forbidding them from worshipping the idol 'Ba'l'. Most of them denied him, so he warned them, and Allah preserved good praise for him among later generations.
Al-An'aam 6:85; As-Saaffaat 37:123-132

articles.x: A righteous prophet whom Allah favored above the worlds and counted among the good. The Qur'an mentioned him among the prophets without detailing his story.

b.v: A righteous prophet whom Allah favored above the worlds and counted among the good. The Qur'an mentioned him among the prophets without detailing his story.
Al-An'aam 6:86; Saad 38:48

articles.x: Dhul-Nun (the Companion of the Fish), sent to the people of Nineveh. He became angry and left in anger before his Lord's permission, so the fish swallowed him in the…

b.v: Dhul-Nun (the Companion of the Fish), sent to the people of Nineveh. He became angry and left in anger before his Lord's permission, so the fish swallowed him in the darkness of the sea. He called upon his Lord in glorification and confession, so Allah saved him, and his people believed, so He let them enjoy life for a while.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:87-88; As-Saaffaat 37:139-148; Yunus 10:98; Al-Qalam 68:48-50

articles.x: A prophet who was the guardian of Maryam (Mary). He called upon his Lord secretly to grant him an heir to inherit from him, though he had reached old age and his wife…

b.v: A prophet who was the guardian of Maryam (Mary). He called upon his Lord secretly to grant him an heir to inherit from him, though he had reached old age and his wife was barren. So Allah gave him the glad tidings of Yahya (John), and made his sign that he would not speak to people for three nights while being sound (in health).
Maryam 19:2-11; Aal-i-Imraan 3:37-41; Al-Anbiyaa 21:89-90

articles.x: Son of Zakariya. Allah gave his father glad tidings of him and made him a chief (sayyid), chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.

b.v: Son of Zakariya. Allah gave his father glad tidings of him and made him a chief (sayyid), chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous. Allah granted him wisdom while still a boy, and dutifulness to his parents, and peace was upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive.
Maryam 19:7-15; Aal-i-Imraan 3:39; Al-Anbiyaa 21:90

articles.x: Son of Maryam (Mary). Allah created him without a father, and he spoke to people in the cradle.

b.v: Son of Maryam (Mary). Allah created him without a father, and he spoke to people in the cradle. Allah gave him the Injil (Gospel) and supported him with miracles by Allah's permission, such as reviving the dead and healing the blind and the leper. He gave glad tidings of a messenger to come after him, and Allah raised him up to Himself; he was not killed nor crucified.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:45-59; Maryam 19:16-34; Al-Maaida 5:110-118; An-Nisaa 4:157-158

articles.x: The Seal of the Prophets and the best of creation. Allah sent him as a mercy to the worlds with the Noble Qur'an, the last of the Books.

b.v: The Seal of the Prophets and the best of creation. Allah sent him as a mercy to the worlds with the Noble Qur'an, the last of the Books. He called to the oneness of Allah (Tawhid) and through him the religion was perfected. He was of great character, and Allah sent him to all of mankind as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner.
Al-Ahzaab 33:40; Al-Anbiyaa 21:107; Al-Fath 48:29; Al-Qalam 68:4; Al-A'raaf 7:158

articles.x: The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is the first and greatest of the pillars of Islam.

b.v: The testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is the first and greatest of the pillars of Islam. Its meaning is to single out Allah alone for worship and to abandon all besides Him, and to affirm the truth of the Prophet ﷺ in what he informed and to obey him in what he commanded. It is the key to Islam, and a servant's Islam is not valid until he utters it, believing in its meaning and acting according to its requirements.
حديث جبريل عن عمر بن الخطاب، رواه مسلم

articles.x: Prayer is the second pillar of Islam; it consists of the five prayers obligatory in the day and night, and it is the first matter for which a servant will be held to…

b.v: Prayer is the second pillar of Islam; it consists of the five prayers obligatory in the day and night, and it is the first matter for which a servant will be held to account on the Day of Resurrection. It is the pillar of the religion and the distinguishing line between a Muslim and a disbeliever. It is obligatory upon every sane, adult Muslim to perform it at its prescribed times, with its conditions and pillars.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والبقرة: 43

articles.x: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam; it is an obligatory due on specified wealth, paid to those entitled to it from the eight categories.

b.v: Zakat is the third pillar of Islam; it is an obligatory due on specified wealth, paid to those entitled to it from the eight categories. It becomes obligatory on wealth when it reaches the nisab (minimum threshold) and a full lunar year has passed over it. It is a purification of wealth and an increase in blessing.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والبقرة: 43

articles.x: Fasting the month of Ramadan is the fourth pillar; it is abstaining from the things that break the fast, from the break of dawn until sunset, as an act of worship to…

b.v: Fasting the month of Ramadan is the fourth pillar; it is abstaining from the things that break the fast, from the break of dawn until sunset, as an act of worship to Allah, the Exalted. It is obligatory upon every sane, adult, and able Muslim, and whoever breaks the fast due to an excuse such as illness or travel must make up the number of days he broke.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والبقرة: 185

articles.t: Hajj to the House (The Fifth Pillar)
articles.x: Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah is the fifth pillar, and it is obligatory once in a lifetime upon whoever is able, physically and financially.

b.v: Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah is the fifth pillar, and it is obligatory once in a lifetime upon whoever is able, physically and financially. It is intending the Ka'bah to perform the well-known rites at a specified time.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ وآل عمران: 97

articles.x: The first of the six pillars of faith, and it includes belief in His existence, Glorified is He, His Lordship, His divinity, His names, and His attributes.

b.v: The first of the six pillars of faith, and it includes belief in His existence, Glorified is He, His Lordship, His divinity, His names, and His attributes. So the servant believes that Allah alone is the Creator, the Provider, the Disposer of all affairs, the One deserving of worship to the exclusion of all others, characterized by the attributes of perfection and exalted above every deficiency.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم

articles.x: The second of the pillars of faith. They are creatures made of light, honored servants who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and who do as they are…

b.v: The second of the pillars of faith. They are creatures made of light, honored servants who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and who do as they are commanded. We believe in their existence and in what has been authentically established of their names, such as Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), and Israfil, and in the tasks Allah has entrusted to them.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والبقرة: 285

articles.x: The third pillar, which is affirming that Allah revealed books to His messengers as guidance for mankind, such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Zabur (Psalms), and the…

b.v: The third pillar, which is affirming that Allah revealed books to His messengers as guidance for mankind, such as the Torah, the Gospel, the Zabur (Psalms), and the Scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham). The Noble Qur'an is the last and greatest of them, and it is the dominant one that abrogates what came before it, and it is obligatory to follow it.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ وآل عمران: 3

articles.x: The fourth pillar, which is affirming that Allah sent to His servants messengers as bearers of glad tidings and warners, the first of them being Noah and the last of…

b.v: The fourth pillar, which is affirming that Allah sent to His servants messengers as bearers of glad tidings and warners, the first of them being Noah and the last of them being Muhammad ﷺ, the Seal of the Prophets. We believe in those of them whom Allah named specifically and in those not named, in general, and we affirm the truth of what they conveyed from Allah.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والنحل: 36

articles.x: The fifth pillar, which is affirming everything that occurs after death: the trial of the grave and its bliss or punishment, the resurrection, the gathering, the…

b.v: The fifth pillar, which is affirming everything that occurs after death: the trial of the grave and its bliss or punishment, the resurrection, the gathering, the reckoning, the scale (mizan), and the bridge (sirat), and Paradise and the Fire. Every person will be recompensed for his deeds.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والحج: 7

articles.t: Faith in Divine Decree, its good and its evil
articles.x: The sixth pillar, which is affirming that Allah knew everything and wrote it, willed everything that occurs, and created everything by His power.

b.v: The sixth pillar, which is affirming that Allah knew everything and wrote it, willed everything that occurs, and created everything by His power. So whatever Allah wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen; nevertheless, the servant has a will and a choice for which he is held accountable, so he has no argument by appealing to divine decree for committing sins.
حديث جبريل، رواه مسلم؛ والقمر: 49

articles.t: Definition and Virtue of the Udhiyah (Sacrifice)
articles.x: The udhiyah is what is slaughtered from grazing livestock (camels, cattle, and sheep) during the days of Eid al-Adha, seeking closeness to Allah the Exalted.

b.v: The udhiyah is what is slaughtered from grazing livestock (camels, cattle, and sheep) during the days of Eid al-Adha, seeking closeness to Allah the Exalted. It is among the rites of Islam; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فصلِّ لربك وانحر﴾. It is a revival of the practice (sunnah) of the Prophet of Allah Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and in it is glorification of Allah, gratitude for His blessings, and generosity toward one's family and the poor.
الكوثر: 2 والحج: 34؛ والإسلام سؤال وجواب

articles.x: The udhiyah is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah mu'akkadah) for one who is able to afford it, according to the majority of scholars, and it is not obligatory — this is what…

b.v: The udhiyah is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah mu'akkadah) for one who is able to afford it, according to the majority of scholars, and it is not obligatory — this is what Shaykh Ibn Baz preferred, citing as evidence the Prophet's ﷺ continual practice of sacrificing every year. Abu Hanifah held that it is obligatory upon the resident who has sufficient means. So whoever leaves it while being able to afford it has missed out on a great good, but there is no sin upon him.
فتوى ابن باز [خلاف: الجمهور سنة مؤكدة، وأبو حنيفة على وجوبها]

articles.t: The Time for Slaughtering the Udhiyah
articles.x: The time for slaughtering begins after the Eid al-Adha prayer; whoever slaughters before the prayer, it does not count as valid for him, due to his ﷺ saying: «من ذبح قبل…

b.v: The time for slaughtering begins after the Eid al-Adha prayer; whoever slaughters before the prayer, it does not count as valid for him, due to his ﷺ saying: «من ذبح قبل الصلاة فإنما هو لحمٌ قدّمه لأهله». According to the most correct view, it extends for four days: the day of Eid and the three days of Tashreeq, ending at sunset of the thirteenth day.
حديث البراء (متفق عليه)؛ وفتوى ابن باز [خلاف: الجمهور ينتهي بغروب 12]

articles.t: What Is Recommended When Slaughtering the Udhiyah
articles.x: It is recommended for the one performing the sacrifice to say the tasmiyah and takbir, saying: «بسم الله، والله أكبر», and if he adds after that: «اللهم هذا منك ولك…

b.v: It is recommended for the one performing the sacrifice to say the tasmiyah and takbir, saying: «بسم الله، والله أكبر», and if he adds after that: «اللهم هذا منك ولك، اللهم تقبّل مني», this is good. It is also recommended to face the sacrificial animal toward the qiblah, to sharpen the blade, and to be kind and gentle toward the animal, due to his ﷺ saying: «فإذا ذبحتم فأحسنوا الذِّبحة».
حديث شدّاد بن أوس، رواه مسلم؛ وفتوى ابن باز

articles.t: What the Person Offering the Sacrifice Avoids During the First Ten Days of Dhul-Hijjah
articles.x: Whoever intends to offer a sacrifice (udhiyah), once the month of Dhul-Hijjah begins, refrains from taking anything from his hair, his nails, or his skin until he offers…

b.v: Whoever intends to offer a sacrifice (udhiyah), once the month of Dhul-Hijjah begins, refrains from taking anything from his hair, his nails, or his skin until he offers the sacrifice, because of the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «إذا أُهِلَّ هلالُ ذي الحجة فلا يأخذنّ من شعره ولا من أظفاره شيئاً حتى يُضحّي». This is specific to the one offering the sacrifice, not to those on whose behalf the sacrifice is offered.
حديث أم سلمة، رواه مسلم؛ وفتوى ابن باز [خلاف: الجمهور على الكراهة، والحنابلة على التحريم]

articles.t: Dividing the Meat of the Sacrifice
articles.x: It is recommended for the one offering the sacrifice to eat from his sacrifice, to give some of it as a gift, and to give charity to the poor from it; and it is best to…

b.v: It is recommended for the one offering the sacrifice to eat from his sacrifice, to give some of it as a gift, and to give charity to the poor from it; and it is best to divide it into three parts: a third he eats, a third he gives as a gift, and a third he gives in charity. This division is recommended, not obligatory, so if he ate all of it or gave most of it in charity, it would still be sufficient for him.
الحج: 28؛ وفتوى ابن باز

articles.t: Conditions of the Sacrificial Animal: Age and Soundness
articles.x: It is a condition that it be from grazing livestock (bahimat al-an'am), and that it reach the recognized age: al-jadha' from sheep is that which has completed six…

b.v: It is a condition that it be from grazing livestock (bahimat al-an'am), and that it reach the recognized age: al-jadha' from sheep is that which has completed six months, al-thaniyy from goats is that which has completed one year, from cattle that which has completed two years, and from camels that which has completed five years. And it must be free from defects, because of his ﷺ saying: «أربعٌ لا تجوز: العوراء البيّن عورها، والمريضة البيّن مرضها، والعرجاء البيّن ظَلَعها، والعجفاء التي لا تُنقي».
حديث البراء (أبو داود والترمذي، صححه الألباني)

articles.x: The pilgrim performing Umrah bathes, applies perfume, and wears the Ihram garments (an izar and rida' for men), then makes the intention to enter the rite at the Miqat.

b.v: Ihram and Intention

The pilgrim performing Umrah bathes, applies perfume, and wears the Ihram garments (an izar and rida' for men), then makes the intention to enter the rite at the Miqat. It is not permissible to pass the Miqat without Ihram.
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ عُمْرَةً
The Talbiyah
The pilgrim begins reciting the Talbiyah, raising his voice with it (for men), and repeats it often from the moment of Ihram until he begins the Tawaf, at which point he stops.
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ لَبَّيْكَ، لَبَّيْكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ لَبَّيْكَ، إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ وَالنِّعْمَةَ لَكَ وَالْمُلْكَ، لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ
Tawaf Around the Ka'bah — Seven Circuits

He circles the Ka'bah seven times in a state of purity, beginning at the Black Stone, touching it or pointing to it while saying 'Allahu Akbar,' keeping the House on his left. He should recite much remembrance and supplication, including what is said between the Yemeni Corner and the Black Stone:
رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
Praying Two Rak'ahs Behind the Station of Ibrahim
After finishing the Tawaf, he prays two rak'ahs behind the Station of Ibrahim if possible, reciting Surat al-Kafirun after al-Fatihah in the first rak'ah and Surat al-Ikhlas in the second.
وَاتَّخِذُوا مِنْ مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى
Sa'i Between Safa and Marwah

He goes out to Safa, climbs it, faces the Qiblah, raises his hands, says 'Allahu Akbar,' and supplicates. Then he descends to Marwah; men should walk briskly between the two green markers, completing seven circuits, the last ending at Marwah. Among what is said upon Safa and Marwah:

اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ، أَنْجَزَ وَعْدَهُ، وَنَصَرَ عَبْدَهُ، وَهَزَمَ الْأَحْزَابَ وَحْدَهُ
Shaving or Trimming the Hair
After the Sa'i, a man shaves his entire head (which is better) or trims all of it, while a woman trims a fingertip's length from her hair. With this, the Umrah is complete.

articles.x: On the morning of the eighth day, he enters Ihram for Hajj, makes the intention, and recites the Talbiyah.

b.v: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhul-Hijjah)

On the morning of the eighth day, he enters Ihram for Hajj, makes the intention, and recites the Talbiyah. Then he goes out to Mina, where he prays Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha, and Fajr, shortening the four-rak'ah prayers without combining them, and spends the night of the ninth there.
لَبَّيْكَ اللَّهُمَّ حَجًّا
The Day of Arafah (9th of Dhul-Hijjah) — The Standing

After sunrise, he travels to Arafah, where he prays Dhuhr and Asr shortened and combined at the earlier time. Then he devotes himself to remembrance and supplication, facing the Qiblah with hands raised, until sunset. The entire area of Arafah is a place of standing, except for the valley of Uranah.
لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
Muzdalifah — Spending the Night

After sunset at Arafah, he proceeds calmly to Muzdalifah, where he prays Maghrib and Isha combined at the later time, and spends the night there. He gathers the pebbles for stoning the Jamarat, prays Fajr early, then remembers Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram until daylight appears.
The Day of Sacrifice — Stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah
He arrives at Mina and stones the large Jamrat al-Aqabah with seven pebbles thrown in succession, saying 'Allahu Akbar' with each pebble. He stops reciting the Talbiyah when he begins the stoning.
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
The Sacrificial Animal and Shaving

After the stoning, the one performing Tamattu' or Qiran slaughters the sacrificial animal, then shaves his head or trims it (shaving is better), while a woman trims a fingertip's length. With this, the first release from Ihram occurs, making everything permissible except relations with women.
Tawaf al-Ifadah (A Pillar of Hajj)

He goes down to Makkah and performs Tawaf al-Ifadah, seven circuits, then walks Sa'i between Safa and Marwah as the Sa'i of Hajj. With this, the second release from Ihram occurs, making everything permissible.
The Days of Tashriq — Spending the Night and Stoning

He spends the nights of Tashriq at Mina, and stones the three Jamarat each day after the sun passes its zenith: the small one, then the middle one, then al-Aqabah, seven pebbles for each. Whoever hastens leaves after stoning on the twelfth day; whoever delays also stones on the thirteenth.
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
The Farewell Tawaf
If the pilgrim wishes to leave Makkah, he makes his last act at the House the Farewell Tawaf of seven circuits. It is waived for a menstruating woman or one in postpartum bleeding.

articles.x: He intends in his heart to remove the state of ritual impurity (the intention is not spoken aloud), and says the name of Allah (Bismillah) when starting.

b.v: Intention and Saying Bismillah
He intends in his heart to remove the state of ritual impurity (the intention is not spoken aloud), and says the name of Allah (Bismillah) when starting.
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
Washing the Hands
He washes his hands three times.
Rinsing the Mouth and Nose
He rinses his mouth and draws water into his nose, then expels it, doing this three times, combining mouth-rinsing and nasal inhalation.
Washing the Face
He washes his face three times, lengthwise from the hairline down to the bottom of the chin, and widthwise from ear to ear.
Washing the Arms to the Elbows
He washes his arms up to the elbows three times, the right then the left.
Wiping the Head and Ears
He wipes his entire head once, starting from the front of the head to the back of the neck, then returns his hands back, then wipes his ears.
Washing the Feet to the Ankles
He washes his feet up to the ankles three times, the right then the left, running his fingers between the toes.
The Supplication After Wudu
When he finishes his ablution, he says the transmitted (reported) remembrance.
أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ. اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْنِي مِنَ التَّوَّابِينَ وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنَ الْمُتَطَهِّرِينَ

articles.x: He faces the qiblah and intends the prayer in his heart, then raises his hands level with his shoulders and says the takbir (Allahu Akbar).

b.v: The Opening Takbir (Takbiratul-Ihram)
He faces the qiblah and intends the prayer in his heart, then raises his hands level with his shoulders and says the takbir (Allahu Akbar).
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
The Opening Supplication (Du'a al-Istiftah)
He places his right hand over his left on his chest, then recites the opening supplication silently.
سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ
Seeking Refuge and the Basmalah
He seeks refuge from Satan (Ta'awwudh) and says the Basmalah silently before reciting al-Fatihah.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
Reciting al-Fatihah
He recites Surah al-Fatihah, which is a pillar (rukn) in every rak'ah, then recites what is easy from the Qur'an in the first two rak'ahs, and after it says: Ameen.

بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ، الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ، الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ، مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ، إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ، اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ، صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
Ruku' (Bowing) and Its Glorification
He raises his hands, says the takbir, and bows, placing his palms on his knees and straightening his back level, and glorifies Allah three times.
سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْعَظِيمِ
Rising from Ruku'
He raises his head, raising his hands as well, saying the tasmi' (Sami' Allahu liman hamidah), and once he is standing upright, he says the tahmid (Rabbana wa lakal-hamd).
سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ، رَبَّنَا وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ
Sujud (Prostration) and Its Glorification

He says the takbir and prostrates on the seven body parts (the forehead and nose, the two palms, the two knees, and the tips of the toes), glorifies Allah three times, and makes abundant supplication.
سُبْحَانَ رَبِّيَ الْأَعْلَى
Sitting Between the Two Prostrations
He rises from prostration saying the takbir, sits in the iftirash position, and supplicates, then prostrates a second time just like the first.
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي، رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي
The Tashahhud
After the first two rak'ahs and at the end of the prayer, he sits for the tashahhud, points with his index finger, and recites the tahiyyat.

التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
The Ibrahimic Blessing (As-Salat al-Ibrahimiyyah)
In the final tashahhud, he sends blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ, then supplicates with whatever he wishes before the taslim (ending salutation).

اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
The Taslim (Closing Salutation)
He concludes the prayer with the taslim, turning to his right then to his left.
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ

articles.x: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.

b.v: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
Al-Baqarah 2:201

رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا، رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا، رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ، وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا، أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ

Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or fall into error. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
Al-Baqarah 2:286
رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً، إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ
Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Truly, You are the Bestower.
Aal-Imran 3:8
رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
Aal-Imran 3:16
رَبَّنَا ظَلَمْنَا أَنْفُسَنَا وَإِنْ لَمْ تَغْفِرْ لَنَا وَتَرْحَمْنَا لَنَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ
Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we shall surely be among the losers.
Al-A'raf 7:23
رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِنْ لِسَانِي يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي
My Lord, expand my breast for me, make my task easy for me, and untie the knot from my tongue so that they may understand my speech.
رَبِّ زِدْنِي عِلْمًا
My Lord, increase me in knowledge.
رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا
Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and offspring comfort to our eyes, and make us leaders for the righteous.
Al-Furqan 25:74
رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
Our Lord, accept [this] from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.
Al-Baqara 2:127
رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَا أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ

Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation [in submission] to You. And show us our rites [of worship] and accept our repentance. Indeed, You are the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
Al-Baqara 2:128
رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
Our Lord, pour upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
Al-Baqara 2:250
رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ لِيَوْمٍ لَّا رَيْبَ فِيهِ، إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ
Our Lord, surely You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allāh does not fail in His promise."
Aal-i-Imraan 3:9
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِن لَّدُنكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً، إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ
My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:38
رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا بِمَا أَنزَلْتَ وَاتَّبَعْنَا الرَّسُولَ فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ
Our Lord, we have believed in what You revealed and have followed the messenger [i.e., Jesus], so register us among the witnesses [to truth]."
Aal-i-Imraan 3:53
رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا فِي أَمْرِنَا وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا وَانصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
Our Lord, forgive us our sins and the excess [committed] in our affairs and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:147
رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَٰذَا بَاطِلًا سُبْحَانَكَ فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
Our Lord, You did not create this aimlessly; exalted are You [above such a thing]; then protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:191
رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ مَن تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ، وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ مِنْ أَنصَارٍ
Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire - You have disgraced him, and for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:192
رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي لِلْإِيمَانِ أَنْ آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنَّا، رَبَّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ عَنَّا سَيِّئَاتِنَا وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ الْأَبْرَارِ

Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller [i.e., Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ)] calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die among the righteous.
Aal-i-Imraan 3:193
رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا مَا وَعَدتَّنَا عَلَىٰ رُسُلِكَ وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ
Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in [Your] promise."
Aal-i-Imraan 3:194
رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ
Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.
Al-Maaida 5:83
رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا مَعَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ
Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people.
Al-A'raaf 7:47
رَبَّنَا أَفْرِغْ عَلَيْنَا صَبْرًا وَتَوَفَّنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
And you do not resent us except because we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and let us die as Muslims [in submission to You]."
Al-A'raaf 7:126
رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ وَنَجِّنَا بِرَحْمَتِكَ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
Upon Allāh do we rely. Our Lord, make us not [objects of] trial for the wrongdoing people And save us by Your mercy from the disbelieving people.
رَبِّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ أَنْ أَسْأَلَكَ مَا لَيْسَ لِي بِهِ عِلْمٌ، وَإِلَّا تَغْفِرْ لِي وَتَرْحَمْنِي أَكُن مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ
My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.

رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ الْمُلْكِ وَعَلَّمْتَنِي مِن تَأْوِيلِ الْأَحَادِيثِ، فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَنتَ وَلِيِّي فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ، تَوَفَّنِي مُسْلِمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ

My Lord, You have given me [something] of sovereignty and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Creator of the heavens and earth, You are my protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous."
Yusuf 12:101
رَبِّ اجْعَلْنِي مُقِيمَ الصَّلَاةِ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِي، رَبَّنَا وَتَقَبَّلْ دُعَاءِ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ

My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and [many] from my descendants. Our Lord, and accept my supplication. Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers the Day the account is established."
Ibrahim 14:40-41
رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا
My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.
Al-Isra 17:24
رَبِّ أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ وَأَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ وَاجْعَل لِّي مِن لَّدُنكَ سُلْطَانًا نَّصِيرًا
My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and to exit a sound exit and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.
Al-Israa 17:80
رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا
Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance.
Al-Kahf 18:10
أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:83
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
There is no deity except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:87
رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ
My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors.
Al-Anbiyaa 21:89
رَبِّ أَنزِلْنِي مُنزَلًا مُّبَارَكًا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الْمُنزِلِينَ
And say, 'My Lord, let me land at a blessed landing place, and You are the best to accommodate [us].'"
Al-Muminoon 23:29
رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَن يَحْضُرُونِ
My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me.
Al-Muminoon 23:97-98
رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
Indeed, there was a party of My servants who said, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.'
Al-Mu'minun 23:109
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ وَارْحَمْ وَأَنتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and You are the best of the merciful.
Al-Muminoon 23:118
رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ، إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا
Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell. Indeed, its punishment is ever adhering; Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and residence.
Al-Furqaan 25:65-66
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ وَاجْعَل لِّي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ وَاجْعَلْنِي مِن وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ

[And he said], "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous. And grant me a mention [i.e., reputation] of honor among later generations. And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure.
Ash-Shu'araa 26:83-85
رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَدْخِلْنِي بِرَحْمَتِكَ فِي عِبَادِكَ الصَّالِحِينَ

My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to do righteousness of which You approve. And admit me by Your mercy into [the ranks of] Your righteous servants.
An-Naml 27:19
رَبِّ إِنِّي ظَلَمْتُ نَفْسِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي
My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.
Al-Qasas 28:16
رَبِّ نَجِّنِي مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ
My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.
Al-Qasas 28:21
رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.
Al-Qasas 28:24
رَبِّ انصُرْنِي عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْمُفْسِدِينَ
My Lord, support me against the corrupting people.
Al-Ankaboot 29:30
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ
My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous."
As-Saaffaat 37:100
رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَّحْمَةً وَعِلْمًا فَاغْفِرْ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمْ عَذَابَ الْجَحِيمِ
Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who have repented and followed Your way and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.
Al-Ghaafir 40:7

رَبِّ أَوْزِعْنِي أَنْ أَشْكُرَ نِعْمَتَكَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَالِدَيَّ وَأَنْ أَعْمَلَ صَالِحًا تَرْضَاهُ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِي، إِنِّي تُبْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ

My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.
Al-Ahqaf 46:15
رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِالْإِيمَانِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِّلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ رَءُوفٌ رَّحِيمٌ
Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.
Al-Hashr 59:10
رَبَّنَا عَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ أَنَبْنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ

Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than Allāh. We have denied you, and there has appeared between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in Allāh alone" - except for the saying of Abraham to his father.
Al-Mumtahana 60:4
رَبَّنَا لَا تَجْعَلْنَا فِتْنَةً لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا رَبَّنَا، إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ
Our Lord, make us not [objects of] torment for the disbelievers and forgive us, our Lord. Indeed, it is You who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise."
Al-Mumtahana 60:5
رَبَّنَا أَتْمِمْ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا، إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent.
At-Tahrim 66:8
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًا
My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house a believer and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction."

articles.x: There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne.

b.v: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ

There is no god but Allah, the Magnificent, the Forbearing. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Noble Throne.
Agreed upon — al-Bukhari and Muslim

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ غَلَبَةِ الدَّيْنِ وَقَهْرِ الرِّجَالِ

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from worry and grief, I seek refuge in You from incapacity and laziness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice and miserliness, and I seek refuge in You from being overcome by debt and overpowered by men.
Al-Bukhari
لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
There is no god but You; glory be to You. Truly, I have been among the wrongdoers.
Al-Anbiya 21:87 — the dua of Dhun-Nun
حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
Aal-Imran 3:173
اللَّهُمَّ رَحْمَتَكَ أَرْجُو فَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
O Allah, it is Your mercy that I hope for, so do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye. Set right all my affairs. There is no god but You.
Abu Dawud (graded hasan by al-Albani)

articles.x: O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your grace so that I need none besides You.

b.v: اللَّهُمَّ اكْفِنِي بِحَلَالِكَ عَنْ حَرَامِكَ، وَأَغْنِنِي بِفَضْلِكَ عَمَّنْ سِوَاكَ
O Allah, suffice me with what You have made lawful against what You have forbidden, and enrich me by Your grace so that I need none besides You.
At-Tirmidhi (hasan)
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا
O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, wholesome provision, and deeds that are accepted.
Ibn Majah (sahih)
رَبَّنَا أَنْزِلْ عَلَيْنَا مَائِدَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ تَكُونُ لَنَا عِيدًا لِأَوَّلِنَا وَآخِرِنَا وَآيَةً مِنْكَ، وَارْزُقْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ
Our Lord, send down to us a table spread with food from heaven, to be a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers.
Al-Ma'idah 5:114

articles.x: My Lord, have mercy on them both as they raised me when I was small.

b.v: رَبِّ ارْحَمْهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرًا
My Lord, have mercy on them both as they raised me when I was small.
Al-Isra 17:24
رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ
Our Lord, forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day the reckoning is established.
Ibrahim 14:41
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ
My Lord, forgive me, my parents, whoever enters my house as a believer, and all the believing men and women.

articles.x: O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to Your covenant and promise as much as I can.

b.v: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَىٰ عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ

O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I hold to Your covenant and promise as much as I can. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge before You Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
Al-Bukhari — the master supplication for forgiveness
أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
I seek the forgiveness of Allah, besides whom there is no god, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all, and I turn to Him in repentance.
At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud (hasan)
رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَتُبْ عَلَيَّ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ
My Lord, forgive me and accept my repentance. Truly, You are the Accepter of repentance, the Most Merciful.
At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud (sahih)
رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الرَّاحِمِينَ
Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy on us, and You are the best of the merciful.
Al-Mu'minun 23:109

articles.x: O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and contentment.

b.v: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالتُّقَىٰ وَالْعَفَافَ وَالْغِنَىٰ
O Allah, I ask You for guidance, piety, chastity and contentment.
Muslim

اللَّهُمَّ أَصْلِحْ لِي دِينِي الَّذِي هُوَ عِصْمَةُ أَمْرِي، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي دُنْيَايَ الَّتِي فِيهَا مَعَاشِي، وَأَصْلِحْ لِي آخِرَتِي الَّتِي فِيهَا مَعَادِي، وَاجْعَلِ الْحَيَاةَ زِيَادَةً لِي فِي كُلِّ خَيْرٍ، وَاجْعَلِ الْمَوْتَ رَاحَةً لِي مِنْ كُلِّ شَرٍّ

O Allah, set right for me my religion, which is the safeguard of my affairs; set right for me my worldly life, in which is my livelihood; and set right for me my Hereafter, to which is my return. Make life for me an increase in every good, and make death a rest for me from every evil.
Muslim
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْجَنَّةَ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ النَّارِ
O Allah, I ask You for Paradise and seek refuge in You from the Fire.
Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah (sahih)
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
O Allah, I ask You for well-being in this world and in the Hereafter.
Ibn Majah and at-Tirmidhi (hasan)
يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَىٰ دِينِكَ
O Turner of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion.
At-Tirmidhi (sahih)
اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَىٰ ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You, and to worship You well.
Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i (sahih)

articles.x: We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah. All praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is…

b.v: أَصْبَحْنَا وَأَصْبَحَ الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، رَبِّ أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَخَيْرَ مَا بَعْدَهُ، وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ وَشَرِّ مَا بَعْدَهُ

We have entered the morning and the dominion belongs to Allah. All praise is for Allah. There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and His is all praise, and He has power over everything. My Lord, I ask You for the good of this day and the good of what follows it, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of this day and the evil of what follows it.
Muslim — in the evening say: أَمْسَيْنَا وَأَمْسَى الْمُلْكُ لِلَّهِ
اللَّهُمَّ بِكَ أَصْبَحْنَا، وَبِكَ أَمْسَيْنَا، وَبِكَ نَحْيَا، وَبِكَ نَمُوتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ النُّشُورُ
O Allah, by You we enter the morning and by You we enter the evening, by You we live and by You we die, and to You is the resurrection.
At-Tirmidhi (hasan)
اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَصْبَحَ بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ أَوْ بِأَحَدٍ مِنْ خَلْقِكَ فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
O Allah, whatever blessing has come to me this morning, or to any of Your creation, is from You alone, with no partner. So Yours is all praise and Yours is all thanks.
Abu Dawud (hasan)

اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَصْبَحْتُ أُشْهِدُكَ وَأُشْهِدُ حَمَلَةَ عَرْشِكَ وَمَلَائِكَتَكَ وَجَمِيعَ خَلْقِكَ، أَنَّكَ أَنْتَ اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُكَ وَرَسُولُكَ

O Allah, this morning I call You to witness, and I call to witness the bearers of Your Throne, Your angels and all Your creation, that You are Allah — there is no god but You alone, with no partner — and that Muhammad is Your servant and Your Messenger.
Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi

articles.x: O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge and Your strength by Your power, and I ask You of Your immense grace.

b.v: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ، وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ، وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ، فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ، وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ، وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ، وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ، وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ

O Allah, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge and Your strength by Your power, and I ask You of Your immense grace. For You are able and I am not, You know and I do not, and You are the Knower of all that is hidden. O Allah, if You know this matter to be good for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affairs, then decree it for me, make it easy for me and bless it for me. And if You know this matter to be bad for me in my religion, my livelihood and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree good for me wherever it may be, then make me content with it.
Al-Bukhari

articles.x: Glory be to the One who has made this subservient to us, for we could not have done it ourselves, and to our Lord we shall surely return.

b.v: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ، وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَىٰ، اللَّهُمَّ هَوِّنْ عَلَيْنَا سَفَرَنَا هَذَا وَاطْوِ عَنَّا بُعْدَهُ، اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ الصَّاحِبُ فِي السَّفَرِ، وَالْخَلِيفَةُ فِي الْأَهْلِ، اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمَنْظَرِ، وَسُوءِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ فِي الْمَالِ وَالْأَهْلِ

Glory be to the One who has made this subservient to us, for we could not have done it ourselves, and to our Lord we shall surely return. O Allah, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness, piety and deeds that please You. O Allah, make this journey easy for us and fold up its distance. O Allah, You are the Companion on the journey and the Guardian of the family. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a sorrowful sight, and from an evil turn of affairs in wealth and family.
Muslim
اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ وَعْثَاءِ السَّفَرِ، وَكَآبَةِ الْمُنْقَلَبِ، وَالْحَوْرِ بَعْدَ الْكَوْرِ، وَدَعْوَةِ الْمَظْلُومِ، وَسُوءِ الْمَنْظَرِ فِي الْأَهْلِ وَالْمَالِ
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of travel, from a sorrowful return, from decline after growth, from the supplication of the oppressed, and from an evil sight in family and wealth.
Muslim
أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
Muslim

articles.x: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of…

b.v: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ ٱلرَّحْمَـٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ٱهْدِنَا ٱلصِّرَٰطَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgement. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us along the straight path — the path of those You have blessed, not of those who incurred wrath, nor of those who went astray.
Al-Fatihah 1:1-7

articles.x: Allah — there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him.

b.v: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلْحَىُّ ٱلْقَيُّومُ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ لَّهُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِى يَشْفَعُ عِندَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَىْءٍ مِّنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا وَهُوَ ٱلْعَلِىُّ ٱلْعَظِيمُ

Allah — there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what lies before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Throne extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation does not weary Him. He is the Most High, the Magnificent.
Al-Baqarah 2:255

articles.t: The last two verses of Surah Al-Baqarah
articles.x: The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers.

b.v: ءَامَنَ ٱلرَّسُولُ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِن رَّبِّهِ وَٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ كُلٌّ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَمَلَـٰٓئِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّن رُّسُلِهِ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ ٱلْمَصِيرُ لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا ٱكْتَسَبَتْ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِن نَّسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِنَا رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ وَٱعْفُ عَنَّا وَٱغْفِرْ لَنَا وَٱرْحَمْنَا أَنتَ مَوْلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرْنَا عَلَى ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلْكَـٰفِرِينَ

The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers. Each one believes in Allah, His angels, His books and His messengers: we make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they say: We hear and we obey. Grant us Your forgiveness, our Lord; to You is the return. Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity: it gets what it has earned and bears what it has brought upon itself. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or fall into error. Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear. Pardon us, forgive us and have mercy on us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.
Al-Baqarah 2:285-286

articles.x: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.

b.v: قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّمَدُ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.
Al-Ikhlas 112:1-4

articles.x: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow upon…

b.v: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ مِن شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ وَمِن شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ وَمِن شَرِّ ٱلنَّفَّـٰثَـٰتِ فِى ٱلْعُقَدِ وَمِن شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ

Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak, from the evil of what He has created, from the evil of darkness when it settles, from the evil of those who blow upon knots, and from the evil of an envier when he envies.
Al-Falaq 113:1-5

articles.x: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer who whispers into the breasts of mankind…

b.v: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ ٱلنَّاسِ مَلِكِ ٱلنَّاسِ إِلَـٰهِ ٱلنَّاسِ مِن شَرِّ ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ ٱلَّذِى يُوَسْوِسُ فِى صُدُورِ ٱلنَّاسِ مِنَ ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ
Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer who whispers into the breasts of mankind, from among jinn and men.

articles.t: The opening verses of Surah Al-Baqarah
articles.x: Alif, Lam, Mim. This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-conscious — those who believe in the unseen, establish the prayer, and spend out…

b.v: الٓمٓ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَـٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ وَبِٱلْـَٔاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ أُولَـٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ وَأُولَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ

Alif, Lam, Mim. This is the Book about which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-conscious — those who believe in the unseen, establish the prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them; and who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and are certain of the Hereafter. Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.
Al-Baqarah 2:1-5

articles.t: Seeking refuge from the evil of what He created
articles.x: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.

b.v: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from the evil of what He has created.
Sahih Muslim

articles.t: The ruqyah of Jibril (peace be upon him)
articles.x: In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allah heal you.

b.v: بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ يُؤْذِيكَ، مِنْ شَرِّ كُلِّ نَفْسٍ أَوْ عَيْنِ حَاسِدٍ، اللَّهُ يَشْفِيكَ، بِاسْمِ اللَّهِ أَرْقِيكَ
In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye. May Allah heal you. In the name of Allah I perform ruqyah for you.
Sahih Muslim

articles.t: Dua for the healing of the sick
articles.x: O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the affliction and grant healing — You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves behind no illness.

b.v: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ، أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ، اشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي، لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ، شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
O Allah, Lord of mankind, remove the affliction and grant healing — You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves behind no illness.
Agreed upon (al-Bukhari and Muslim)

articles.t: Protection from every devil and vermin
articles.x: I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every harmful eye.

b.v: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ، مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ، وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah from every devil and every venomous creature, and from every harmful eye.
Sahih al-Bukhari

articles.x: In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.

b.v: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ، وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
In the name of Allah, with whose name nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi

articles.x: Al-isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) is a sunnah when beginning recitation, and its wording is: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم».

b.v: Al-isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) is a sunnah when beginning recitation, and its wording is: «أعوذ بالله من الشيطان الرجيم». The basmalah is recited at the beginning of every surah except Surat at-Tawbah. Between two surahs, the reciter has several permissible ways of reciting.
أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ — بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin clearly, from its point of articulation, without an audible ghunnah (nasal sound), when it is followed by one of the six guttural…

b.v: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin clearly, from its point of articulation, without an audible ghunnah (nasal sound), when it is followed by one of the six guttural letters: hamzah (ء), ha (ه), 'ayn (ع), ha (ح), ghayn (غ), and kha (خ).
مِنْ خَيْرٍ — يَنْأَوْنَ — مِنْ عِلْمٍ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: If, in a separate word, one of the letters of «يَنْمُو» (ya, nun, mim, waw) follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is merged (idgham) into it while the ghunnah is…

b.v: If, in a separate word, one of the letters of «يَنْمُو» (ya, nun, mim, waw) follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is merged (idgham) into it while the ghunnah is retained for the duration of two harakahs (counts).
مَن يَقُولُ — مِن وَالٍ — فَمَن يَعْمَلْ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: If the letter lam or ra follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is fully merged into it without ghunnah, and this only occurs between two separate words.

b.v: If the letter lam or ra follows the sakinah nun or tanwin, the nun is fully merged into it without ghunnah, and this only occurs between two separate words.
مِن لَّدُنْهُ — مِن رَّبِّهِمْ — غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: Converting the sakinah nun or tanwin into a concealed mim when it meets the letter ba, while observing the ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs; it has only one…

b.v: Converting the sakinah nun or tanwin into a concealed mim when it meets the letter ba, while observing the ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs; it has only one letter, which is ba.
مِنۢ بَعْدِ — أَنۢبِئْهُم — سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin in a manner between idhhar (clear pronunciation) and idgham (merging), free of shaddah (doubling), while the ghunnah is retained…

b.v: Pronouncing the sakinah nun or tanwin in a manner between idhhar (clear pronunciation) and idgham (merging), free of shaddah (doubling), while the ghunnah is retained for the duration of two harakahs. It has fifteen letters (the letters remaining after those of idhhar, idgham, and iqlab).
مِنكُمْ — أَنصَارَ — جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: One of the rulings of the sakinah mim: if the letter ba follows it, it must be concealed with a labial concealment (ikhfa shafawi), with ghunnah for the duration of two…

b.v: One of the rulings of the sakinah mim: if the letter ba follows it, it must be concealed with a labial concealment (ikhfa shafawi), with ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs. It is called 'labial' because both mim and ba are articulated from the two lips.
تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ — وَهُم بِالْآخِرَةِ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: If a moving (voweled) mim follows the sakinah mim, the first is merged into the second with ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs, becoming a single doubled (shaddah)…

b.v: If a moving (voweled) mim follows the sakinah mim, the first is merged into the second with ghunnah for the duration of two harakahs, becoming a single doubled (shaddah) mim; this is called 'the minor idgham of two identical letters' (idgham al-mithlayn al-saghir).
لَهُم مَّا يَشَاءُونَ — كَم مِّن فِئَةٍ
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: If any letter other than ba and mim follows the sakinah mim, the mim must be pronounced with a clear labial idhhar, without ghunnah.

b.v: If any letter other than ba and mim follows the sakinah mim, the mim must be pronounced with a clear labial idhhar, without ghunnah. The greatest care against concealing it must be taken before the letters fa and waw.
أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ — عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ — هُمْ فِيهَا
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: The madd (prolongation) without which the letter itself cannot stand, and which does not depend on a hamzah or a sukun; it is prolonged for the duration of two harakahs.

b.v: The madd (prolongation) without which the letter itself cannot stand, and which does not depend on a hamzah or a sukun; it is prolonged for the duration of two harakahs. The letters of madd are: alif preceded by a fathah, waw preceded by a dammah, and ya preceded by a kasrah.
قَالَ — يَقُولُ — قِيلَ — نُوحِيهَا
تحفة الأطفال

articles.x: That a hamzah comes after a letter of madd within a single word; its ruling is obligatory, and it is prolonged for four or five harakahs whether continuing (wasl) or…

b.v: That a hamzah comes after a letter of madd within a single word; its ruling is obligatory, and it is prolonged for four or five harakahs whether continuing (wasl) or pausing (waqf), and six when pausing if the hamzah is at the end of the word.
